description:
**Sites:** `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:2792-2794` (`check_count_caps`, backend-canonical) and `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:849-851` (`check_space_count_limits`, handler defense-in-depth pre-flight).

Both helpers construct the cap-exceeded `overQuota` SetError with the same format:

```rust
SetError::new(SetErrorType::OverQuota).with_description(format!(
    "{label}: would have {proposed} after adding {add} (existing {current}, cap {cap})"
))
```

The four `{label}` values are the four aggregate names (`roles`, `members`, `channels`, `categories`). The `{cur*}` values are read from the Space object the backend just fetched; `{cap}` is read from the per-account `ChatLimits` returned by `ChatBackend::limits()`. The description string reaches the remote client verbatim via `set_error_value` → `notUpdated.<id>` (`space.rs:1095-1100` for the handler path, `memory.rs:1201-1202` for the direct-backend-call path).

**What goes wrong (information disclosure):**

The wire description discloses three pieces of deployment-private state to any caller who can pass the `Space/set` permission gate enough to trip the cap check:

1. **Deployment policy cap** — the operator-configured per-account / per-tier cap value for that aggregate. Workspace AGENTS.md "Backend caps and limits" §"No spec contract on values" is explicit: *"caps are NOT spec-mandated. New extensions SHOULD NOT add cap-advertising fields to their JMAP capability objects."* The same policy edit (jmap-chat-spec commit `80d5e11`, bd:JMAP-kt5k) deliberately dropped `maxGroupMembers` / `maxSpaceMembers` / `maxRolesPerSpace` / `maxChannelsPerSpace` / `maxCategoriesPerSpace` from `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat` to prevent exactly this surface. Re-introducing the cap value through an `overQuota` description undoes that posture: any caller who can issue `Space/set` can probe the cap by submitting an over-cap add and reading `cap {cap}` from the failure response. The cap becomes implicitly client-queryable despite the spec edit.

2. **Current per-Space aggregate count** — `existing {current}` reveals `space.roles.len() / .members.len() / .channels (uncategorized + categorized).len() / .categories.len()`. For `members`: a Space membership list is a permission-gated property on draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space (a non-member calling `Space/get` does not get the full `members` array in any spec-compliant projection — and indeed chat-server filters non-member-non-previewable visibility at `space.rs:391-399`). The overQuota response back-channels the member count to a caller who cannot enumerate members directly. The same applies to `roles` / `channels` / `categories` for callers who lack the relevant read permission but have a (different) write-side permission that lets them propose an Add* patch.

3. **Tier identification via cap inference** — multi-tenant SaaS deployments that vary `ChatLimits` per tier (the AGENTS.md backend-caps-and-limits §"Args are plumbed even when the default ignores them" explicit example: Free vs Pro) expose the caller's account tier through the cap value. A cross-tenant probe (e.g., a federation peer or a sock-puppet account in a different tenant) reading the `cap {cap}` value distinguishes Free / Pro / Enterprise tiers without an enumeration endpoint.

**Spec / standard mechanism the kit should use instead:**

The right path for client-visible caps is the JMAP Quota extension (`urn:ietf:params:jmap:quotas`) — workspace AGENTS.md §"Backend caps and limits" §"Client visibility, when desired" calls this out explicitly. Quota records are explicitly meant for advertising dynamic caps + usage to authorized clients. They are read-permission-gated separately, so the kit can surface caps to authorized clients without back-channeling them through `/set` error descriptions to any caller with write permission. RFC 8620 §5.3 `overQuota` semantics do not require the description to name the limit value.

**Fix shape (defer to /do-beads):**

Replace the variable-bearing description with a static string per aggregate name, e.g. `SetError::new(SetErrorType::OverQuota).with_description("too many roles")` / `"too many members"` / `"too many channels"` / `"too many categories"`. Keep `SetErrorType::OverQuota` as the typed surface — that is the spec-defined channel for cap-exceeded. Drop `{current}` / `{add}` / `{proposed}` / `{cap}` from the wire entirely. The label-as-static-string still tells a client *which* aggregate to retry without; numeric counts and caps are deployment-private.

Apply at both sites (memory.rs:2792 + space.rs:849) so the canonical-template propagation rule does not regress when other extension-server siblings adopt the same per-aggregate cap pattern. The handler-side description and backend-side description should be byte-identical for response-shape parity. Add an integration-test canary asserting (a) the response type is overQuota, (b) the description does NOT match any of \$cap-bearing-numeric-substrings or '`existing`' / '`cap`' literals.
title: overQuota descriptions leak per-Space counts + deployment caps to any caller who can propose a /set patch
